branding.title: Branding
branding.intro: The logo and accent colour of this installation. The footer stays as it is.
branding.logoHint: SVG, PNG or WebP, at most {max, number} KB. Appears in the header and on the sign-in page.
branding.accentHint: One colour value. The server builds the light and dark steps from it and checks the contrast while doing so — a colour that would make the interface unreadable is refused. The block type colours are left alone: they mean something.

members.title: Members
members.linkOnItsWay: The sign-in link is on its way.
members.noMailSetUp: No mail delivery is configured. Pass this link on in person — whoever opens it is signed in as {email}.

mail.title: Mail delivery
mail.intro: Sign-in links and invitations go this way. Without delivery, only somebody who already has a passkey can get in.
mail.fromEnvironmentNotice: Some values come from the server's environment and cannot be changed here. They are in the installation's .env.

transport.consoleHint: No delivery. Sign-in links end up in the log — anybody who can read it can get into any account.
transport.noneHint: Sign-in links only exist through the command line.

mail.graphIntro: You need an app registration in Entra ID with the application permission Mail.Send and admin consent.
mail.secretStored: stored — leave empty to keep it
mail.testIntro: Whether a relay works shows when something is sent. Otherwise the first attempt is somebody's sign-in link — and a failure then looks like a broken account.
mail.testSent: Sent to {email}. If nothing arrives: check the spam folder.

agenda.addDayNote: Add a note about the day

drag.droppedWithTime: {title} dropped {where}, position {position, number}, new start time {time}.
drag.landedWithTime: {title} lands {where}, position {position, number}, new start time {time}.

field.legacyHint: These values come from an earlier version of this block type. They are kept, but can no longer be edited.
field.richTextReadOnly: Contains formatting. Editing comes with the text editor — until then the content here stays untouched.

agenda.noFields: This block type has no further fields.
agenda.offline: No connection. Your changes will be sent as soon as it is back.
agenda.parkHint: Take it out of the schedule without deleting it
agenda.parkedHint: Belongs to the day, does not count towards the time.

guest.title: Invitation to {workshop}
guest.intro: Enter the e-mail address this invitation was sent to. The link works only with that address.
guest.rejected: That does not match. Check the address the invitation was sent to.
guest.tooMany: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
guest.invalidTitle: This invitation is no longer valid
guest.invalidBody: The link was withdrawn, has run out, or never existed. Whoever invited you can send a new invitation.

login.title: Sign in to GoodWorkshop
login.intro: No password. Either with a passkey or through a link by e-mail.
login.passkeyUnavailable: Passkeys need HTTPS and are not available on this address. The sign-in link by e-mail works.
login.passkeyFailed: The passkey could not be confirmed.
login.sentBody: If there is an account for that address, a sign-in link is on its way. It is valid for {minutes, plural, one {one minute} other {# minutes}}.
login.linkExpired: This link has expired or has already been used. Ask for a new one.
login.linkIncomplete: The link was incomplete. Ask for a new one.

setup.title: Set up GoodWorkshop
setup.intro: This installation has nobody who can administer it yet. Enter yourself as the first administrator — everything else, mail delivery included, happens in the interface afterwards.
setup.emailHint: This is how you will sign in from now on. You invite other people in the interface afterwards.
setup.keyHint: It is in the server log:
setup.linkHere: No mail delivery is configured yet, so the sign-in link is here. It works once and then expires.
setup.linkSent: The sign-in link is on its way. Check your inbox.

errors.conflict: Somebody else has changed this workshop in the meantime.

brand.notHex: Please give a colour as a hex value, e.g. #7c3aed.
brand.grey: Grey has no hue to build an accent colour from. Pick something with colour in it.
brand.contrastOnBrand: In {theme, select, light {light} dark {dark} other {}} mode this shade only reaches {ratio}:1 for text on the accent surface. 4.5:1 is required.
brand.contrastSubtle: In {theme, select, light {light} dark {dark} other {}} mode this shade only reaches {ratio}:1 for muted text on a muted surface. 4.5:1 is required.
brand.checkNameAndColour: Please check the name and the colour.

collab.unavailable: The collaboration service is unreachable. Nothing can be written without it, because that would mean two write paths onto the same day.

folder.intoItself: A folder cannot sit inside itself.
folder.targetGone: There is no such target folder.
folder.intoOwnDescendant: A folder cannot go into one of its own subfolders.
folder.nameTaken: There is already a folder of that name in there.
folder.grantTooWide: You can only hand on what you hold yourself.
folder.creatorHasAccess: Whoever made the folder already has access.

logo.unsupportedType: SVG, PNG and WebP are allowed.
logo.tooLarge: The logo may be at most {max, number} KB (this file: {actual, number} KB).
logo.notSvg: That does not look like an SVG file.
logo.unsafeActive: The SVG contains {what}. Export it without scripts and without interactivity — most programs call that “plain SVG”.
logo.unsafeExternal: The SVG points outwards via {what}. Export it with fonts and images embedded, without external references.
logo.unsafeDoctype: The SVG contains {what}. Export it without a DTD and without entities.
logo.typeMismatch: The file does not match the format it claims.

mail.noSmtpUrl: Transport SMTP, but no SMTP URL is configured — neither in the environment nor in the settings.
mail.transportNone: Transport “no delivery”: no mail can be sent. Use `node scripts/cli.mjs login-link --email …` or pick a transport in the settings.
mail.graphMissing: Transport Microsoft Graph, but {field} is missing.

member.adminOnly: Only tenant admins may manage members.
member.invalidEmail: That is not a valid e-mail address.
member.lastAdmin: That is the last active admin. Make somebody else an admin first — otherwise nobody can reach the administration any more.
member.checkEmailAndRole: Please check the e-mail address and the role.

setup.wrongKey: That setup key is not correct.
setup.invalidEmail: That is not a valid e-mail address.
setup.alreadyClaimed: This installation already has an administrator.
setup.identityFailed: The identity could not be created.

sharing.ownerHasAccess: The owner already has full access.

sharing.tooManyInvites: Too many invitations in a short time. Wait a minute.

tags.createFailed: The tag “{name}” could not be created.

token.nameRequired: Give the token a name — otherwise you will not know later what it was for.
token.nameTooLong: The name may be at most {max, number} characters long.
token.noScopes: A token with no scopes can do nothing. Pick at least one.

workshop.forbidden: You do not have permission for that: {capability}
workshop.versionConflict: The workshop has changed in the meantime (expected {expected}, found {actual}).
workshop.unknownModuleType: There is no such block type.

errors.failed: That did not work. Try again.

errors.forbidden: You do not have permission for that.

mail.checkSettings: These settings do not fit together.

passkey.notYours: This passkey does not belong to your account.

errors.setupFailed: Setup failed. The details are in the log.

bin.emptyHint: What lands here stays until somebody removes it for good.
bin.purgeWarning: This removes {title} with all its days and blocks. There is no way back.

drag.instructions: Drag onto a folder to move it. With the keyboard: the button next to it opens a list to pick from.

library.emptyFilteredHint: Another search, another folder or another tag.
library.emptyHint: Create one — the first day comes with it.
library.name: Name
library.removeFolder: Remove the folder — its contents move up one level

magicLink.subject: Your sign-in link for GoodWorkshop
magicLink.body:
Hello,

here is your sign-in link:
{link}

It is valid for {minutes, plural, one {one minute} other {# minutes}} and works once only.

If you did not ask for this, you can ignore this message —
nothing happens without the link.

shareInvite.subject: Invitation to the agenda: {workshop}
shareInvite.body:
Hello,

you are invited to see the agenda of "{workshop}".

{link}

The link will ask for your e-mail address. Enter {email} — only that address opens the agenda.

You do not need an account for this.

test.subject: GoodWorkshop: test message
test.body:
This message confirms that mail delivery works.

Sign-in links and invitations now go the same way.

settings.intro: Your account: language, passkeys and access tokens.

language.title: Language
language.intro: Applies to the interface, your exports and the e-mails you receive.
language.label: Language

passkeys.intro: Sign in without a password, using a fingerprint, your face or a security key. The key itself never leaves your device.
passkeys.needsHttps: Passkeys need HTTPS. This installation runs on {origin}.
passkeys.none: No passkey yet. Until there is, every sign-in goes through a link by e-mail.
passkeys.notConfirmed: The passkey could not be confirmed.
passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.unavailable: This installation runs on {origin}. Browsers only allow passkeys over HTTPS (or on localhost) — none can be created here. The sign-in link by e-mail remains the way in.

settings.title: Settings

tokens.title: Access tokens
tokens.intro: For MCP clients such as Claude Code, Claude Desktop, the Gemini CLI, Codex or Langdock. A token acts as you — it can never do more than you can.
tokens.freshHint: It is shown once only — what is stored is its hash.
tokens.noUserAdmin: User administration is deliberately not on offer: an MCP client must never invite anybody or make anybody an admin.

connect.title: Connect a client
connect.freshNote: Everything here is already filled in — open it, copy, paste.
connect.placeholderNote: Put your own token where gwp_… is. It is shown in full only right after you create it.
connect.claudeCodeStep: Once, in the terminal. Every project knows the server after that.
connect.claudeDesktopStep: Add this to the configuration file and restart Claude Desktop. If "mcpServers" is already there, only the inner part is new.
connect.geminiStep: Once, in the terminal. The entry lands in ~/.gemini/settings.json.
connect.codexStep: Two lines in the terminal. Codex deliberately keeps the token out of its configuration file — the entry names only the environment variable.
connect.codexEnvNote: To make it stick, the first line belongs in your shell configuration (~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc). Otherwise Codex knows the token in this one terminal only.
connect.langdockStep1: Settings → Integrations → MCP → add a connection.
connect.langdockStep4: Paste the bare token as the key — without the word “Bearer”, Langdock adds that itself:

workshop.accessIntro: Editors see changes immediately — they are in the same document. Readers see the schedule but change nothing.

guest.banner: You are looking at this agenda as a guest.
guest.bannerEditor: You are looking at this agenda as a guest and can edit it.
guest.goneTitle: This agenda is no longer available
guest.goneBody: The access was ended, withdrawn, or has run out. Whoever invited you can send a new invitation.

guests.title: Guests without an account
guests.intro: An invitation goes out by e-mail and works only with that address. Guests see the days of this agenda and nothing else — no library, no folders.
guests.notMailed: No mail delivery is set up. Pass this link on to {email} yourself — it works only with that address:
guests.until: The link is valid until the last day of the agenda.
guests.untilUndated: The agenda has no date yet, so the link is valid until it is withdrawn.
